reason: Material is the complete 2-page AAMAS extended abstract (all sections incl. conclusion read; no appendix exists). The absence of data, tables and mechanism detail is the paper's own property, not missing material; scored under frozen anchor A1 (no reported experiment -> E items not_reported). In scope as a minimal A-type claim: LLM-generated goals/code are validated in the environment, retained and reused.

paper.central_claim: A BDI-LLM architecture with an Automated Evolution Module (variation, selection, inheritance) lets software agents autonomously evolve goals, reasoning and executable code from experience; a prototype shows agents can discover goals and generate executable behaviours from minimal prior knowledge, with limits in behavioural inheritance and stability.
paper.title: Self-Evolving Software Agents

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref not exposed to the worker; null by contract.

evidence.quote: combining BDI reasoning with LLMs to enable autonomous evolution of goals, reasoning, and executable code.
evidence.support_explanation: Central claim: evolve goals, reasoning and code.

evidence.quote: Autonomous agents can adapt their behaviour to changing environments, but remain bound to requirements, goals, and capabilities fixed at design time, preventing genuine software evolution.
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap: design-time fixed goals/capabilities. Conceptual; no measured failure of a baseline.

evidence.quote: However, existing agentic AI approaches largely rely on prompt-driven behaviour and externally defined objectives, providing limited support for structured, long-term evolution.
evidence.support_explanation: Nearest-neighbour statement without any named LLM-agent self-evolution baseline or citation.

evidence.quote: it initiates an automated software evolution cycle based on variation, selection, and inheritance.
evidence.support_explanation: Only description of the evolution mechanism's structure; operations of variation/selection/inheritance are not specified.

evidence.quote: The agent is initially provided only with a textual description of the environment and a minimal set of APIs, without predefined domain-specific knowledge or goals.
evidence.support_explanation: Prototype setting; environment is Deliveroo.js-inspired multi-agent game.

evidence.quote: In such cases, the agent autonomously generates new goals, revises its reasoning structures, and synthesizes executable actions, which are then validated through interaction with the environment. Successful behaviours are retained and reused in subsequent situations, while ineffective ones are discarded.
evidence.support_explanation: Only statement of the selection and retention rule: environment validation, keep successes, discard failures; no criteria, store, or versioning described.

evidence.quote: Preliminary experiments show that the agent is able to autonomously discover operational goals and generate executable behaviours starting from minimal prior knowledge.
evidence.support_explanation: Qualitative statement of results; no numbers, baselines, runs or tables in the text.

evidence.quote: At the same time, the results highlight current limitations of LLM-driven evolution, particularly in terms of behavioural inheritance and robustness as environmental complexity increases.
The evolution module is triggered when perceived information cannot be interpreted or exploited using the current knowledge and goal structures.
By isolating evolution from the reasoning loop, the architecture preserves behavioural coherence while enabling autonomous, long-term evolution of the agent’s internal structure.
evidence.support_explanation: Coherence-preservation claim stated as design property, not tested; contradicted by the reported inheritance/robustness limits.

evidence.quote: These challenges point to the need for reinforcement mechanisms, memory consolidation, and more robust selection strategies.
evidence.support_explanation: Authors concede that retention/selection are not yet adequate.

evidence.quote: Future work will focus on strengthening inheritance and long-term consistency, extending the evaluation to more complex multi-agent scenarios
evidence.support_explanation: Evaluation scope is a single prototype setting.

evidence.quote: We implemented a prototype of the proposed self-evolving agent using a BDI control loop extended with an LLM-driven evolution module
evidence.support_explanation: A prototype exists; model/prompt/code are not described in the read text.

signatures.object: The agent's knowledge/reasoning structures, goals and executable actions/plans (non-weight, BDI agent code)
signatures.information: Perceptions from a dynamic multi-agent environment, current knowledge and goal structures; textual environment description and minimal API only at start
signatures.operation: Evolution module (LLM) generates new goals, revises reasoning structures and synthesizes executable actions when current structures cannot interpret percepts
signatures.output: new goals, reasoning updates and executable behaviours
signatures.conditions: Triggered by percepts not interpretable by existing knowledge/goals
signatures.feedback: Interaction with the environment (success or failure of behaviours)
signatures.selection_rule/data: Validated through environment interaction; successful kept, ineffective discarded (criteria and data not specified)
signatures.persistence: Retained and reused in later situations; storage form, versioning and inheritance mechanism not described
signatures.later_use: Reused in subsequent situations (mechanism not described)
signatures.claimed_effect: Autonomous discovery of goals and generation of executable behaviours from minimal prior knowledge (qualitative)
signatures.failure_boundary: Behavioural inheritance and robustness degrade as environmental complexity grows

gap.author_gap: Agents and self-adaptive systems adapt but cannot evolve requirements, goals and capabilities fixed at design time; agentic AI is prompt-driven with externally defined objectives.
gap.checked_gap: A real conceptual limitation, but stated at a generic level without a demonstrated failure of a baseline and without any LLM-agent nearest neighbour (skill/memory/code self-improvement agents) in the text.
gap.lineage: Software evolution/self-adaptive systems -> BDI agents -> LLM code generation; LLM-based self-improving agents are not discussed in the read text.
gap.closest_adjacent: Not identifiable from the text: no named self-evolving LLM agent or skill-library work is cited.
gap.residue: Autonomous revision of goals and code with preserved coherence.
gap.method_response: Separate evolution module with variation-selection-inheritance acting on knowledge, goals and actions.
gap.unresolved: Novelty against LLM-agent self-evolution literature cannot be assessed from this extended abstract.

rs_pattern.reason: Considered generative_process_redesign (fixed component -> free design variable) and assumption_audit_and_pivot (audit and relax a load-bearing assumption); neither tactic is executed: there is no iterative generative procedure with a measured quality/efficiency payoff, and no assumption audit with a re-derived guarantee or constructed counterexample. The operation is an architectural proposal for LLM-driven goal/code evolution with environment validation. Still fully evaluated.

matches.condition_checks: Gap-triggered synthesis of executable actions validated by environment and retained (S1 partially, trigger and keep/discard stated); no execution tests, repair loop, library, or reuse ablation reported.
Self-generated goals resemble self-directed practice, but no verified-new-skill admission, curriculum or coverage evidence.

unassigned: Evolution of goals and BDI reasoning structures (not only skills/tools) has no direct domain card; single weak-evidence case, no revision proposed.

expectations.applies_when: Executable artifacts are admitted for reuse
expectations.reason: Environment validation is claimed as the gate, but tests, success criteria and invocation evidence are not described.

expectations.applies_when: Retained library claimed to carry the gain
expectations.reason: No retained-artifact ablation or any quantitative result.

expectations.applies_when: Artifact forging sits inside a larger architecture
expectations.reason: Question: is the executable artifact isolated and tested? Behaviour generation is embedded in a full BDI-LLM architecture with no isolated test.
Reuse conditions of retained behaviours are not described; authors report inheritance failures as complexity grows.
Expect environment, metrics, number of runs and failures; none present in the text (evaluated scope: Sec 3-4, no appendix).

expectations.applies_when: Coherence or stability of evolved behaviour claimed
expectations.reason: Design-level coherence claim is contradicted by the authors' own report of weak behavioural inheritance and robustness.

claims.text: Agents can autonomously discover goals and generate executable behaviours from minimal prior knowledge (feasibility).
claims.setting: Single prototype in a Deliveroo.js-inspired multi-agent environment
claims.counterevidence: No quantified results; the instability they report limits the claim
claims.allowed_conclusion: Existence claim only; unverifiable from the text.

claims.text: Isolating the evolution module preserves behavioural coherence and enables long-term evolution.
claims.counterevidence: Authors report poor behavioural inheritance and robustness
claims.allowed_conclusion: Not supported; partially contradicted by the authors.

claims.text: Successful behaviours are retained and reused while ineffective ones are discarded.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Stated design intent; retained improvement not shown.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: A proposed BDI-LLM architecture and a prototype whose qualitative feasibility is asserted. Below even the task level (no measured output or score is reported in the text), so no retained or improver conclusion is possible.
assessment.unresolved: All quantitative evidence; retention mechanism; novelty versus LLM-agent self-evolution work; stability.

G.reason: A genuine but generic conceptual limitation (goals and capabilities fixed at design time) cited to software-engineering sources; no demonstrated failure of a baseline and no LLM-agent nearest neighbour compared, so between the 0 and 2 anchors.

M.reason: Variation-selection-inheritance applied to knowledge, goals and actions is a recognisable idea, but operations, signals, assumptions and distinguishable predictions are not given; self-claimed coherence is contradicted by reported inheritance problems.

X.reason: Trigger, environment-validation and keep/discard are named, but selection criteria, persistence form, versioning, rollback, conflict handling and later reading are not described, and authors concede selection and consolidation are weak.

E.measurement.reason: Anchor A1: no metric, benchmark or validator is reported; the single sentence on preliminary experiments gives no measurement.
search_scope: whole 2-page extended abstract; no tables, figures with data, or appendix

E.causality.reason: No ablation, baseline or alternative explanation is tested; no store-off or evolution-off comparison.

E.holdout.reason: No selection/test separation, held-out environment or contamination discussion is reported.

E.statistics.reason: No run counts, variance, failure denominators or uncertainty are given.

E.cost.reason: No LLM calls, tokens, time or evolution cost are reported.

rationale: 两页扩展摘要：BDI-LLM 演化模块提出目标/代码自演化，仅称环境验证后保留成功行为；无数据、无对照，作者自认继承与稳定性不足。E 项按 A1 记 not_reported。
